pr.title: Ban `ArrayToPointer` and `MutToConstPointer` from runtime MIR
pr.description:
Zulip conversation: <https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/stream/189540-t-compiler.2Fwg-mir-opt/topic/CastKind.3A.3APointerCoercion.20in.20Runtime.20MIR/near/443955195>

Apparently MIR borrowck cares about at least one of these for checking variance.

In runtime MIR, though, there's no need for them as `PtrToPtr` does the same thing.

(Banning them simplifies passes like GVN that no longer need to handle multiple cast possibilities.)

r? mir
pr.author: scottmcm

processing.reason: This PR is a MIR-cleanup/optimization that normalizes the runtime-nop coercions `PointerCoercion(ArrayToPointer)` and `PointerCoercion(MutToConstPointer)` into `CastKind::PtrToPtr` in `CleanupPostBorrowck`, then bans residual variants post-borrowck (Validator `fail!`) and turns lingering uses in codegen/const-eval into `bug!` (compiler ICEs). The transformation is explicitly semantics-preserving: the PR, the frozen analysis, and the decoded MIR dumps all describe these casts as runtime no-ops whose constant-eval behavior was "a NOP immediate copy" and whose codegen was already pointer-cast-like. There is no wrong value computation to encode: replacing the coercion kind with `PtrToPtr` yields identical pointer values, and the only observable "failure" under the historical behavior would be a compiler ICE (panic/bug!), not a different program result. Manufacturing a pair whose functions differ by an arbitrary return-value change would be an unrelated rewrite, which the instructions forbid. Therefore no source-grounded original/transformed pair can be validated to produce different defined values under O0/O3 and Miri.

analysis.summary: After borrowck, `ArrayToPointer` and `MutToConstPointer` pointer coercions are runtime nops and are normalized to `CastKind::PtrToPtr` by `CleanupPostBorrowck`; `Validator` rejects any residual occurrence at/after `Analysis(PostCleanup)`. This lets runtime passes such as `GVN` handle only ordinary pointer casts, and MIR dumps from `InstSimplify`/`SimplifyCfg` accordingly show `PtrToPtr`.
analysis.originalLogic: Runtime MIR retained `PointerCoercion(ArrayToPointer)` and `PointerCoercion(MutToConstPointer)` as distinct cast kinds after borrowck. `GVN` explicitly accepted `PointerCoercion::MutToConstPointer | PointerCoercion::ArrayToPointer | PointerCoercion::UnsafeFnPointer` in its pointer-cast evaluation and collapsed `PtrToPtr | PointerCoercion(MutToConstPointer)`; const-eval treated the two coercions as a NOP immediate copy, and codegen handled them like pointer casts.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: The pre-PR behavior left `PointerCoercion(ArrayToPointer)` / `PointerCoercion(MutToConstPointer)` in post-borrowck runtime MIR, requiring every downstream pass to recognize those additional variants (or to normalize only some of them). Under the new invariant, the correct transformation is to rewrite every such `Rvalue::Cast` assignment to `CastKind::PtrToPtr` in `CleanupPostBorrowck` and reject residual variants after borrowck; retaining them is the historical behavior being eliminated, not a demonstrated miscompile.
analysis.inputDomain: MIR bodies containing pointer coercions/casts: raw-pointer mutability changes (`*mut T` to `*const T`) and array-to-pointer coercions (`[T; N]` or references to arrays to `*mut T`/`*const T`), especially in runtime MIR after borrowck (e.g. casts such as `x as *mut u8 as *const u8` and `&mut arr as *mut [T; N] as *mut T`).
analysis.trigger: An `Rvalue::Cast` with `CastKind::PointerCoercion(ArrayToPointer | MutToConstPointer)` reaches `CleanupPostBorrowck`, or survives into any MIR phase at/after `Analysis(PostCleanup)`.
preconditions: The MIR phase is at or after `Analysis(PostCleanup)` (runtime MIR); before that, borrowck still needs the distinct coercion kinds.
The statement is an assignment of the form `Rvalue::Cast(kind, ..)` where `kind` is `PointerCoercion::ArrayToPointer` or `PointerCoercion::MutToConstPointer`.
At runtime the coercion is a pointer-level NOP, so `PtrToPtr` is semantically equivalent.
pitfalls: Do not normalize these casts before borrowck: the source notes borrowck uses the distinction to know whether to check lifetimes in pointees (variance).
A residual `PointerCoercion(ArrayToPointer|MutToConstPointer)` in runtime MIR is treated as a compiler bug; codegen and const-eval now use `bug!` rather than silently accepting it.
The equivalence to `PtrToPtr` is runtime-only; replacing too early loses borrowck-relevant information.
Normalizing only `MutToConstPointer` while leaving `ArrayToPointer` (or vice versa) is incomplete under the new invariant.
Changed test expectations in `InstSimplify`/`SimplifyCfg` dumps are consequences of earlier normalization, not evidence that those passes themselves changed behavior.
analysis.testStrategy: Inspect `-Zdump-mir`/mir-opt diffs around `CleanupPostBorrowck`: the same cast should appear as `PointerCoercion(ArrayToPointer|MutToConstPointer)` before cleanup (or in Initial MIR) and as `PtrToPtr` after. Exercise `fn roundtrip(x: *const u8) -> *const u8 { x as *mut u8 as *const u8 }` from `tests/mir-opt/instsimplify/casts.rs`, the array casts in `tests/mir-opt/retag/array_casts.rs`, and pre-codegen slice iterators (`tests/mir-opt/pre-codegen/slice_iter.*`). Assert that `Validator` reports no post-borrowck residual coercion, and compare paired functions whose only difference is whether the cast is `ArrayToPointer`/`MutToConstPointer` versus `PtrToPtr`.
evidence: Apparently MIR borrowck cares about at least one of these for checking variance.
In runtime MIR, though, there's no need for them as `PtrToPtr` does the same thing.
(Banning them simplifies passes like GVN that no longer need to handle multiple cast possibilities.)
BorrowCk needed to track whether these cases were coercions or casts,
to know whether to check lifetimes in their pointees,
so just make them ordinary pointer casts instead.
The following are allowed in [`AnalysisPhase::Initial`] as they're needed for borrowck,
but after that are forbidden (including in all phases of runtime MIR):
Both are runtime nops, so should be [`CastKind::PtrToPtr`] instead in runtime MIR.
